title: bug(console): the agent-key generator reports a 200 that carried no key as `Request failed (200)` — a transport failure that did not happen
body:
Split out of objectui#7980 by the `domain:ui` PM seat, exactly as that card's maintainer ruling (comment 5583988475, director seat, decision batch #91) directs: *"The `!data?.key`-on-200 arm (`Request failed (200)`) is a separate, determinate wording defect: the seat files it as its own `pm:queue` card, ⛔ not held behind this one."*

objectui#7980 itself is now held behind the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` gate (its ruled fix exports a symbol from a published index ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`). **This half is not**, which is the whole point of the split.

## Measured

`apps/console/src/pages/developer/AgentConnectSection.tsx`, around line 119:

```ts
const json = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
const data = json?.data;
if (!res.ok || !data?.key) {
  throw new Error(json?.error?.message || `Request failed (${res.status})`);
}
```

The condition is a disjunction, so the second arm — **`!data?.key` on a response that was `ok`** — reaches the same `throw`. With no `error.message` in the body, the template interpolates the real status:

⇒ a **200** whose body simply carried no key is reported to the developer as **`Request failed (200)`**.

The request did not fail. Nothing about the transport went wrong. The sentence names the one layer that is known to have worked.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

The thrown string lands in `setError(...)` and is the **entire** report the developer gets. objectui#7980's triage measured the cost of this class on its third facet: an agent or a developer reading "request failed" goes and investigates the transport, which is the wrong layer, and a wrong pointer is more expensive than no pointer. Here the misdirection is unusually stark because the status in the message is `200`.

## What is asked

1. Split the condition so the two failure modes produce **two different sentences**. The `!res.ok` arm keeps today's behaviour. The `ok`-but-no-key arm says what actually happened: the server answered successfully and the response carried no key.
2. ⛔ The new arm must not reuse the `Request failed (${res.status})` string, and ⛔ must not report a status as evidence of a transport failure.
3. Pin both arms, with the 200-without-key case as its own test carrying a lit control (a neighbouring assertion known to fire on the same command shape), so a zero is a reading.

## Not asked

⛔ Anything about `error.userMessage` or `error.code` — that is objectui#7980 and it is gated. Do not import, export, or write a local copy of `readEnvelopeFailureText` on this card; leave the `json?.error?.message` read exactly as it is. ⛔ Not a Clause-② card: no published surface moves, no acceptance set widens.

## Re-check

```
sed -n '105,127p' apps/console/src/pages/developer/AgentConnectSection.tsx
grep -rn "Request failed (" apps packages --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts
```

## Dedup

⚠️ Declared rather than hidden: this is a **split of a card whose thread already carries the dedup work** — objectui#7980's filing ran the family search and named #7959, #7938 / PR #7960, #7368, #4634 as related-not-duplicate, and no card in that set carries the 200-arm. ⚠️ This repo's `search_issues` has measured false zeros, so no independent zero would have added evidence.

Related: objectui#7980 (parent, and the ruling that ordered this split) · objectui#7959 · objectstack ADR-0112.
